summary:
BioBeacon puts you in the boots of an astronaut testing a new and applied health monitoring system on the Moon. As you explore the lunar surface, the mission controls show your biometrics in real time, as well as how your actions affect your body.

The Objective:  Collect all lunar rock samples and stay alive. Manage your oxygen, stamina, sleep, and stress, all while staying clear of hazards such as radiation and pressure hotspots.

The Next Frontier:  Our HUD can display real-life data using an ESP32 and the sensors we wired to it. Aside from simulating the made-up biometrics, we can use measurements such as body temperature, CO2 levels, and heart rate taken from the ESP32 to show your own health data. This shows that this project can be driven by real hardware in designing tools and suits astronauts use and wear to monitor their health.
details:
The project demonstrates how continuous biometric monitoring could help maintain astronaut health during long missions far from Earth. To prove the idea works beyond the screen, we developed a physical sensor kit that transmits readings directly into the simulation.

Our hardware consists of five sensors connected to ESP32. The MAX30102 which monitors heart rate and SpO2, MLX90614 monitors skin temperature, SCD41 for CO2 concentration, and BME280 for suit pressure. Our kit also included an MPU6050 accelerometer to warn about impact warnings, but we omitted it from the simulation since it takes place in the moon with microgravity in effect. The ESP32 collects data from all five sensors. We wrote the code for it in C++ in an Arduino IDE that reads and processes the sensor data. Python scripts then forwards the data to Godot, where we build the 3D astronaut simulation and display the readings on the astronaut’s HUD in real time. The language to make the simulation utilized Godot Engine's native language, GDScript.

BioBeacon's creativity comes from combining physical sensor hardware with an interactive simulation. Our team considered each sensor's capabilities and how relevant they are to astronauts' health.
